description: Medieval Serbian kingdom and later empire (c. 768–1389) under the Nemanjić dynasty that grew from a small Raška principality to dominate the Balkans; Stefan Nemanja's consolidation and monastic building programme, Sava's establishment of the Serbian Autocephalous Church (1219), and Stefan Dušan's imperial proclamation (1346) made medieval Serbia a major Orthodox Christian power before Ottoman expansion dismantled its political structure at Kosovo (1389).

temporal.notes: Stub: dates from GeoJSON basemap years 900–1279

lifecycle_phases.description: Nemanjić dynasty consolidates Raška principality; Stefan Nemanja builds Studenica monastery; 1217 papal coronation creates kingdom
Bela Mrtvačka Serbia controls Bosnia, Zeta, Kosovo; Stefan Dušan conquers Macedonia, Albania, Thessaly; 1346 proclaimed Emperor of Serbs and Greeks
Dušan's empire fragments immediately after his death; Battle of Maritsa (1371) kills Serbian nobles; Ottoman vassal states emerge
Kosovo (1389), mythologised Serbian defeat; Despotate of Serbia survives until Mehmed II's conquest of Smederevo (1459)

rise_factors.description: Dušan's military combining Serbian heavy cavalry with mercenary Catalan infantry and Greek administrative expertise enabled unprecedented Balkan territorial expansion
Serbian Autocephalous Church (established 1219 by Sava) provided ecclesiastical legitimacy independent of Byzantine Constantinople

decline_factors.description: Dušan's imperial title had no institutional basis, his 'empire' was held together by personal authority that his heirs could not replicate
Ottoman military superiority in combined-arms warfare with Janissary infantry and sipahi cavalry consistently defeated Serbian cavalry-dependent forces
